note: Re-measured for Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#31: net +4 from 312. All 4 are unhandled-error (G104) findings on new s.db.Exec(...) DDL calls added to SQLiteStore.migrate()/PostgresStore.migrate() for the new expansion_instances table backing dynamic-node-expansion (.expand()) execution: one CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and one CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS per dialect (store/sqlite.go:241,254 and store/postgres.go:314,327). Same idempotent 'already exists is benign, safe to ignore' pattern as every ALTER TABLE/CREATE INDEX statement immediately above it in the same function, and the same pattern already accepted in every prior baseline bump below. No new finding categories (no G202/SQL-concatenation); the new table's INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT statements are all parameterized (?/$N placeholders). Verified via `gosec -fmt=json ./...` on this branch vs. its origin/main merge base. Temporary ceiling for pre-existing findings. CI must not exceed it; reduce it as findings are remediated. Re-measured for Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#8: net +9 from the prior 302 (verified by diffing gosec JSON output between this branch and its exact merge base, matched on file+rule+code snippet rather than line number, since new lines earlier in store/sqlite.go and store/postgres.go shift every later finding's line number without changing the finding itself). That net +9 is 11 newly-introduced findings offset by 2 findings that only appear 'removed' because the exact query text they match on changed (see item 3 below) — not real fixes. All 11 newly-introduced findings are the same two already-accepted categories from #6/#7's notes above, not new categories of risk: (1) 8 unhandled-error (G104) findings on new s.db.Exec(...) DDL calls added to SQLiteStore.migrate()/PostgresStore.migrate() — 6 for ALTER TABLE runs ADD COLUMN pipeline_version / resumed_from_run_id plus the partial index on resumed_from_run_id (run-definition-snapshot and resume-lineage fields), and 2 for a new CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on pipeline_versions(pipeline_id, version) (closes a compute-then-insert race in SavePipelineVersion that this PR's resolveRunPipelineVersion makes far more likely to trigger — see that function's doc comment in both files). Same idempotent 'already exists is benign, safe to ignore' pattern as every other schema-setup statement in those functions. (2) 1 unhandled-error (G104) finding on api/handlers_pipeline.go's new h.store.SavePipelineVersion(p.ID, ..., "initial version") call in the pipeline Create handler — this is the exact same fire-and-forget style as the pre-existing, still-unguarded SavePipelineVersion call a few lines away in the Update handler; fixing only the new call site while leaving its sibling unguarded would be inconsistent, and error-handling that call site is out of scope for this PR. (3) 2 SQL-string-concatenation (G202) findings, one each in store/sqlite.go's and store/postgres.go's GetLatestRunsByPipelineIDs, are byte-for-byte pre-existing findings at the same locations (both queries already used strings.Join(placeholders, \",\") / a Postgres $N placeholder list for a parameterized IN-clause, not string-interpolated user input) that only re-triggered the snapshot-matching diff because pipeline_version/resumed_from_run_id were appended to both queries' column lists (fixing a real cross-backend inconsistency: Postgres's GetLatestRunsByPipelineIDs previously silently dropped those two new fields to their zero values while SQLite's had already been fixed); not a new SQL-injection surface. Two genuine gosec findings from this PR's own new code were fixed before this baseline update, not reflected in the ceiling: engine/artifact_store.go's LocalDiskArtifactStore initially had a G301 (world/group-readable artifact directory, 0o755 -> 0o750) and 2 G104 (unchecked os.Remove cleanup -> explicit `_ = os.Remove(...)`) findings in its first draft. Re-measured for Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#10: net +1 from 311 (verified the same way — diffed this branch's gosec JSON against its origin/main merge base, which independently re-measures at exactly 311, matching the baseline). The one new finding is a single unhandled-error (G104) on PostgresStore.migrate()'s new `s.db.Exec(...CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scheduler_leader...)` call (store/postgres.go) backing the new PostgresLeaderElector (Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#10) — the exact same idempotent 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in migrate(), already-exists is benign' pattern as every other schema-setup statement in that function and the 8 findings accepted for the same reason above. No G202/SQL-concatenation or other new categories: all of PostgresLeaderElector's/store/postgres_leader.go's queries are parameterized ($1/$2/... placeholders), including the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE upsert.
